mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of linear equations represent coincident lines?
mcqs.explanation: Two lines are coincident when one equation is a non‑zero multiple of the other. In option A, the second equation is exactly twice the first, so both represent the same line. Options B, C and D have the same slope but different intercepts, giving parallel distinct lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate graph position to number of solutions
mcqs.question: When the graphs of two linear equations intersect at a single point, the corresponding system of equations has
mcqs.explanation: If two straight lines intersect at one point, that point satisfies both equations, giving a unique ordered pair (x, y). Hence the system has exactly one solution. Parallel lines give no solution, and coincident lines give infinitely many.

mcqs.question: Which of the following linear equations has its graph passing through the point (2, ‑1)?
mcqs.explanation: Substituting x = 2 into each equation: for A, y = 3(2) – 7 = –1, which matches the given point. Options B, C and D give y = 1, 2 and –2 respectively, so their graphs do not pass through (2, ‑1). This tests the ability to translate an algebraic equation into its graphical location.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand solution of a pair as common point
mcqs.question: The system of equations 3x + 2y = 12 and x – y = 1 has a unique solution. What are the coordinates of the common point?
mcqs.explanation: From x – y = 1, we get x = y + 1. Substituting into 3x + 2y = 12: 3(y + 1) + 2y = 12 ⇒ 5y + 3 = 12 ⇒ 5y = 9 ⇒ y = 9/5. Then x = y + 1 = 9/5 + 5/5 = 14/5. Hence the common point is (14/5, 9/5). Options A, C and D do not satisfy both equations.

mcqs.question: Two straight lines will intersect each other if

options.A: They have the same slope but different intercepts
options.B: They have the same slope and same intercept

mcqs.explanation: Lines with different slopes are not parallel; therefore they must meet at exactly one point. Options A and B describe parallel and coincident lines respectively, while two vertical lines (option D) are parallel and never meet.

mcqs.question: Which condition guarantees that two linear equations represent parallel but distinct lines?
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines have identical slopes; if their y‑intercepts differ, the lines never meet, giving distinct parallel lines. Option A gives coincident lines, C gives intersecting lines, and D gives perpendicular lines.

mcqs.question: Two linear equations represent coincident lines if

options.A: Their slopes are equal but intercepts differ
options.C: One equation is a non‑zero multiple of the other
options.D: They intersect at a right angle

mcqs.answer: One equation is a non‑zero multiple of the other
mcqs.explanation: Coincident lines are exactly the same line; algebraically this means one equation can be obtained by multiplying the other by a non‑zero constant. Option A describes parallel distinct lines, B intersecting lines, and D perpendicular lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate graph position to number of solutions
mcqs.question: If the graphs of two linear equations are parallel and distinct, how many solutions does the system have?
mcqs.explanation: Parallel distinct lines never meet, so there is no ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations simultaneously. Hence the system has no solution. One solution occurs when lines intersect, and infinitely many when they are coincident.
